assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dye-sensitized nanocrystalline TiO2 cells created a new architecture in which light absorption and charge transport are separated, with a mesoporous nanostructured electrode as the enabling materials design. Structure-function logic is clear and the field has spawned thirty years of molecular and interfacial photochemistry.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the decisive contribution; Grätzel is the clear leader. Hagfeldt was a major later contributor and is credited, but I regard the foundational invention as two-person.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, extensively reproduced, commercial niche modules exist and the concept fed directly into perovskite photovoltaics. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit a third person such as Hagfeldt for later developments.
Commercial impact of DSSCs themselves is modest compared with the scientific influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crystal structures of the Mo-Fe protein and the FeMo cofactor, including the central carbide and later turnover-state structures, explain how biological N2 fixation is organised at the atomic level. This is chemistry of enormous importance to the nitrogen cycle, and the structural evidence is of the kind I trust.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the key crystallographic advances (cofactor structure, interstitial carbide, ligand-bound states). Seefeldt (with Dean) supplied mechanistic and biochemical framework. Dean and Ribbe are also strong; fitting this into three is hard.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well established and independently confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction is still incompletely resolved, so recognition may be somewhat early for a mechanism claim.
uncertainties: Mechanistic details of substrate binding at the cofactor remain debated.
Allocation of credit among five contributors is difficult and could look arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes small-molecule action as event-driven induced proximity, with PROTACs and molecular glues such as the thalidomide analogues now in clinical development. It is a conceptual change in drug design with broad uptake.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed the PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto also made important contributions, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with many clinical candidates, but approvals are still limited and the long-term therapeutic record is not yet in. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical success is not yet demonstrated by an approved PROTAC.
Boundary between PROTACs and molecular glues complicates the prize configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, FSM-16, SBA-15) extended molecular-sieve design from micropores to tunable 2-10 nm channels. These materials opened a field of ordered porous solids, and their structures were established through diffraction and electron microscopy. This is close to my own area, so I judge the structural evidence with some confidence.
assessment.attribution: Mobil's Kresge and Beck introduced M41S, Inagaki independently made FSM-16 and Stucky's group generalised the synthesis with SBA-15. Ryoo and Zhao made later important extensions. The priority picture is shared but defensible.
assessment.maturity: Long established with thousands of follow-up studies and commercial relevance in catalysis, adsorption and drug delivery. Discovery dates from the early 1990s, so timing is late rather than early.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil and the Japanese group, and the role of Beck, complicate the trio.
Industrial impact has been narrower than early expectations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent within a decade, linking a simple crystalline structure family to remarkable optoelectronic properties. Strong materials chemistry story with real application pull.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells, Park and Snaith made the decisive solid-state efficiency and stability steps. Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok are also major contributors, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is confirmed independently by many groups, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercialisation remain open.
Many deserving contributors compete for three places.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts, via organic structure-directing agents, new framework types and engineered active sites, connects framework structure to shape-selective catalysis. It is a major structural and materials chemistry achievement with large industrial uses in refining and emissions control.
assessment.attribution: Davis, Zones and Corma span new framework synthesis, structure-directing agent design and catalytic application. Yu, Tsapatsis and others have strong claims, and the field is diffuse with many contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and industrially proven. The difficulty is that it is a broad body of work and not one sharp discovery.
uncertainties: Whether a single clear discovery can be identified within a diffuse field.
Zeolite structure determination, including electron methods, is part of the story but is not directly credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable surface terminations and strong performance in energy storage and electromagnetic shielding. A genuinely new materials family with clear structure-composition-function relationships.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum jointly reported Ti3C2 in 2011 and developed the field; credit is relatively clean. Later leadership is shared with many groups.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely, but practical applications are still emerging and surface chemistry and termination control are not fully understood. Somewhat early.
uncertainties: Real-world applications are not yet established.
Surface termination structure is hard to characterise rigorously.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods made it possible to determine structure and dynamics of proteins in solution at atomic resolution, an enabling method used by a very broad community. The Nobel committee has already honoured NMR once (Ernst, Wüthrich), so I would judge novelty carefully.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay were central to triple-resonance and isotope-labelling methods and to dynamics measurements; Wagner and Palmer are also strong. A three-person configuration is plausible but excludes important names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and robust with decades of independent confirmation; timing is not a concern but the topic partly overlaps earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier NMR prizes may reduce novelty.
Allocation among many method developers is difficult.
